sources._comment: Back to the Office (Shopify, one category 'Computers' for all 142,271 rows on 23 Oct 2026, 29,750 in stock). It sells business IT too (HPE, Cisco, BTI, Origin Storage, POS): only these consumer brands, and no product whose name says server, warranty, spare part ... (lessons L14, L40). Feed 111663 is the same shop's in-stock list: not used, 102827 has the stock of every product. Hotel TVs (Samsung HG.., "Hospitality TV") and network gateway/controllers are out; the same product twice in this shop is shown once, at its lowest price (lessons L47). Fourth dry run (24 Oct 2026): HP "Contract" toner, waste boxes, large-format (DesignJet, 200 ml+) ink and paper, business cameras (VIGI) and outdoor links (CPE) are out (lessons L48). Fifth dry run: outdoor radio links, business firewalls, data-centre disks and adapters without a cable are out (lessons L49). Sixth check (live site after the import, 24 Oct 2026): rack NAS (RackStation), data-centre and enterprise disks (Kioxia CD8/CM7, Kingston DC, Seagate Enterprise, SAS3), HPE parts, broadcast cameras and controllers (Panasonic AW, Sony SRG, Canon RC-IP), production scanners, meeting-room hubs, aggregation switches and campus Wi-Fi are out (lessons L50). The word 'serial' (serial ports and cables) no longer blocks 'Serial ATA', the consumer SSDs and hard disks; data-centre disks (WD Gold, Toshiba MG, Intel D3/D5/D7, Seagate Nytro) stay out. Other business words that stopped consumer products are narrowed: 'blade' (not the Razer Blade laptops), 'rugged' (not LaCie Rugged disks), 'ECC' (not 'Non-ECC' memory), 'server' (not a 'NAS/storage server'), labels and thermal transfer (not label printers); the report counts what each word leaves out. After the second import (24 Oct 2026, lessons L53): privacy screens and filters, cable locks, laptop and monitor risers, USB and Wi-Fi network cards of home brands, Logitech Rugged iPad cases, watch straps, conferencing monitors, unmanaged and desktop/rackmount switches are consumer products; Dell and Lenovo server disks (Dell 345-/400-, Lenovo 4XB7A, S4520, WD DC HC), Synology SAT/SNV5000 disks and DP backup boxes, Canon CR cheque scanners and Brother TJ/RJ industrial label printers are out. After the third import (lessons L54): enterprise and campus switches (NETGEAR M4250/M4300/M4350, Ubiquiti Enterprise Campus ECS/EAV, Zyxel XS3800/XGS4600, QNAP QSW-M7000), Synology HAS (SAS) disks and server lines (PowerEdge, ProLiant, ThinkSystem, PRIMERGY) are out; XPG Lancer Blade memory, 'Reverse Blade' fans, DDR5 memory named ECC and Lenovo 4X90 USB-Ethernet adapters are in. Dry run of 25 Oct 2026 (lessons L64): Office 365 CSP licences ("... [EOS 01.10.23]", end of sale) were on the cameras page because of "EOS", Panasonic Toughbook rugged business computers, HP "LASERJET ENT" enterprise printers, Toshiba MG data-centre disks, Logitech GROUP conference-room cables and HP "SPS-" service parts are out. The feed of 25 Oct says in_stock = 1 with stock_quantity 0 on about 17,300 of the products the plan kept, about as many as the plan has more than the import of 24 Oct (old phones such as the Motorola Moto G30 among them): stockFromQuantity (a row is in stock only with a quantity above 0). Live check after the import of 25 Oct 2026 (lessons L64): server memory (Samsung M321R/M393A/M386A, Lenovo 4X77A/4ZC7A, Kingston Server Premier KSM and the Kingston modules made for Cisco UCS, HP ProLiant, Dell PowerEdge and Lenovo ThinkSystem: KCS-, KTH-PL, KTD-PE, KTL-TS), Toshiba MG09 data-centre disks and accessories of the Panasonic Toughbook ("Panasonic FZ-VNP026U stylus pen", "FZ-BAZ2232 memory module") are out.

Data projectors (Epson EB, installation laser projectors), hotel TVs, photo paper, call-centre headsets and the makers' own replacement power supplies are out (dry run of 24 Oct 2026). Owner, 24 Oct 2026: as many as possible, if safe: more consumer brands, genuine ink and toner, laptop chargers, monitor and TV mounts, and from the catch-all folders ('looseFolders') only products whose name says what they are. sources._comment: PcNova.co.uk (229,625 rows on 25 Oct 2026): the same wholesale catalogue as PCHUB.UK (same count, the same "Default Category>..." folders, names cut at 70 characters, pictures from stockinthechannel.com; rrp_price is price x 1.38, not a real earlier price). It takes PCHUB.UK's rules (rulesFrom). Its product links go to it-supplies.co.uk. The dry run counts how many products no other shop has, and how many are the same product at another price (lessons L63). Owner, 25 Oct 2026 (lessons L64): imported under the name "PcNova (IT-Supplies)", because the shop button opens it-supplies.co.uk; like PCHUB.UK it trusts stock_quantity (inherited).

GamingKit (50,000 rows on 25 Oct 2026, gamingkit.co.uk): the same wholesale catalogue as PCHUB.UK, so it takes PCHUB.UK's rules (rulesFrom). Every row says in_stock = 1 but most say stock_quantity = 0: stockFromQuantity (a row is in stock only with a quantity above 0). Many rows have the made-up EAN 012345678912 and an "Image coming soon" picture; the report counts the same product at two shops (lessons L63). Owner, 25 Oct 2026 (lessons L64): not imported. The dry run showed all of its 4,576 products also at PCHUB.UK, every one dearer, none of its own.
